admission.justification: A call-time fresh scenario produces no forced report refresh.

applicability: UsageReportsScriptTests scenario timestamps used to judge cached usage-report freshness.
conditions: Each case builds its timestamps when it runs; an explicit fetched_at value is preserved.
The fresh/stale contrast uses the production 60-second threshold.
Fresh cases sample the current time; deliberately stale cases subtract five minutes; caller-supplied fetched_at stamps are preserved unchanged.
exclusions: No guarantee that arbitrary execution pauses leave a timestamp fresh forever.

evidence: evidence/item1-controlled-age-before.log fails on base module bytes after a 70-second controlled age (the case's stamp aged past the bridge's 60-second rule); evidence/item1-controlled-age-after.log passes with the identical script on the candidate; evidence/item1-alone-after.log and evidence/item1-module-after.log pass on the final bytes; the case and the 60-second rule arrived with 1ef442f478a118031599a90f9b547adca503d595 (L184), paseo_bridge.mjs:331

statement: A usage-report case takes its fetchedAt stamps when the case runs, so the bridge's 60-second freshness rule is judged against a stamp that is fresh at call time rather than one aged by the module's import-to-execution delay.
